# Usage Guide

[English](usage.md) | [中文](usage.cn.md)

[← Documentation Hub](../README.md) | [Installation Guide](./installation.md) | [Configuration Reference](../reference/configuration.md)

This guide is for projects that have already installed `opencode-for-everything`. All commands assume they run at the source repository root, with `/path/to/project` replaced by the actual project path.

## Configuration Source and Generated Files

`.o4e/` is the sole O4E configuration source. `.opencode/` contains runtime files generated by the builder for OpenCode to read; do not directly edit files managed by this component.

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.o4e/config.jsonc` | Rule files, tools, Skills, Soul, Agent/Workflow loading, and prompt directories |
| `.o4e/agents/all/*.jsonc` | Roles usable as the main Agent or as managed subagents |
| `.o4e/agents/primary/*.jsonc` | Roles usable only as the session's main Agent |
| `.o4e/agents/subagent/*.jsonc` | Roles that run only as subagents and may continue delegating per configuration |
| `.o4e/workflows/*.jsonc` | process-v1 main-session DAGs, structured I/O, Gates, and checkpoint recovery |
| `.o4e/prompts/` | Prompt files in the language selected at install time |
| `.o4e/skills/` | Editable Skill sources registered directly by the plugin; not copied to `.opencode/skills/` |
| `mcp` / `loadMcp` in `.o4e/config.jsonc` | Managed MCP servers and per-Agent MCP tool allowlists |

The default `default` mode preserves the global `defaultModel`, Agent `model`, and `fallbackModels`,
and models may include variants. Managed subtasks preferentially freeze the target configuration candidates, inheriting from the parent Session when unconfigured;
candidates do not trigger automatic model retries or switching — they only feed diagnostics and explicit `resolve` decisions. Only `clear` clears
the current runtime model projection and configuration candidates, without deleting source files. See
[the Model Selection section of the Configuration Reference](../reference/configuration.md#model-selection-and-run-modes).

For the full fields see the [Configuration Reference](../reference/configuration.md), [Agent Reference](../reference/agents.md), and [Workflow Reference](../reference/workflows.md).

MCP is open to managed Agents by default. Servers already present on the host or defined in `mcp` in `config.jsonc` are projected per `loadMcp`; use `{}` or `blockMcp` to disable specific Agents. See [the MCP section of the Configuration Reference](../reference/configuration.md#mcp) for configuration.

## Applying Configuration Changes

After modifying Agent/Workflow JSON, Schemas, tools, Skills, or plugin code, rebuild and restart OpenCode:

```bash
node scripts/installer.mjs build --target /path/to/project
```

Prompt Markdown, Soul, and managed instruction files are re-read at the next relevant system assembly. When you cannot determine the change type, rebuilding is also fine.

## Checking Installation Status

```bash
node scripts/installer.mjs status --target /path/to/project
node scripts/installer.mjs status --global
```

Project-level status checks `.o4e/` and the generated runtime; global status checks the global configuration, runtime, and plugin registration.

## Backing Up and Restoring Configuration

Export the project's editable `.o4e/`:

```bash
node scripts/installer.mjs export my-config.o4e.tar.gz --target /path/to/project
```

The archive contains only `.o4e/`, not the regenerable `.opencode/`. The archive name must end with `.o4e.tar.gz` and must not be saved inside the `.o4e/` being exported. Import and export require the system to provide `tar`; on Windows, prefer `%SystemRoot%\System32\tar.exe`.

After importing configuration, the runtime is rebuilt automatically:

```bash
node scripts/installer.mjs import my-config.o4e.tar.gz --target /path/to/project --force
```

When the target already has `.o4e/`, interactive import asks whether to overwrite; non-interactive import requires `--force`. Import accepts only ordinary, non-link archive files and rejects paths outside `.o4e/`, backslash paths, links, and special files; use only archives from trusted sources. Global configuration also supports import and export:

```bash
node scripts/installer.mjs export my-config.o4e.tar.gz --global
node scripts/installer.mjs import my-config.o4e.tar.gz --global --force
```

## Uninstalling the Runtime

The following **silent uninstall** commands only clean up runtime files generated and recognizable by the component, preserving `.o4e/` and other project files:

```bash
node scripts/installer.mjs uninstall --no-tui --target /path/to/project
node scripts/installer.mjs uninstall --no-tui --global
```

After a project-level uninstall, you can regenerate the runtime from the retained `.o4e/` with `build --target /path/to/project`.

A global uninstall also removes the server plugin registration, and `build --global` only rebuilds files without restoring that registration. The complete way to restore while keeping custom configuration is to first export the retained configuration, then import the same archive; a global import rebuilds and re-registers the plugin. Use a new backup file name and check the target scope before executing:

```bash
node scripts/installer.mjs export retained-global.o4e.tar.gz --global
node scripts/installer.mjs import retained-global.o4e.tar.gz --global --force
```

Do not continue importing after an export failure; before restarting OpenCode you can check registration with `status --global`. Do not overwrite custom configuration with a default `install --force` just to restore registration.

Interactive uninstall's "keep configuration?" defaults to "yes" and, like silent uninstall, preserves `.o4e/`. Only when you actively choose not to keep it and confirm the deletion summary is the entire configuration source deleted; back it up yourself beforehand. See the [CLI uninstall notes](../reference/cli.md).
